summary: China's exports jumped 36% in September on AI-driven chip demand and home-grown AI chips gained ground, but car sales and holiday spending show households staying cautious.
body: China's trade figures for September came in far above forecasts. Exports rose 36.3% from a year earlier and imports rose 31%, giving a monthly trade surplus (exports minus imports) of about $134 billion. The surplus for the first nine months, $938 billion, puts China on course to pass $1 trillion again this year[^1]. Much of the boost came from the global rush to build AI data centres: semiconductor exports more than doubled in the first nine months[^1]. Factory-gate prices, what producers charge for goods, rose 5%, the fastest since mid-2022. A statistics official linked this to commodity prices and AI-related demand. Consumer prices rose only 0.9%[^2].

Chinese-made AI chips are also taking more of the home market. An IDC report seen by Reuters says Nvidia's share of China's data-centre AI chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, with its shipments down 44%. Huawei's share rose to 28%[^3][^4]. US export rules limit which chips Nvidia can sell in China, and Beijing requires Chinese companies to get approval before importing them[^3].

Spending at home looks weaker. Domestic car sales fell 27% in September while car exports rose 64%. AP links the drop to weaker consumer confidence and smaller government subsidies[^5]. During the Golden Week holiday, Reuters calculations show domestic spending per trip fell to its lowest level since 2022, and cinema ticket sales were the weakest since 2014, though more people travelled abroad[^6]. One analyst says the main problem is worry about income and jobs, not an unwillingness to spend[^6]. My read: factories and exports are running fast while households are holding back.

For millions of delivery riders, couriers and ride-hailing drivers, the labour ministry has released China's first nationwide draft rules for gig workers[^7][^8]. Where a platform controls the work, workers would get labour contracts. Net pay could not fall below the local minimum wage, and a person would have to review any decision by an app's algorithm to suspend or ban a worker's account[^7][^8]. Public comments are open until November 8[^8].
